subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MAP draft + technical eval milestone (Acme)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Attached is an updated MAP draft (acme_map_draft_v2.xlsx) with the technical evaluation milestone expanded per our discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference on Acme workloads to inform procurement decision and target deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
- Success criteria needed by Acme: latency and cost envelope, model quality on your benchmarks, and integration path (SSO/data access).

Technical evaluation milestone (proposed) — owners & target dates
- Milestone name: Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks + decision)
- Target completion: 2026-10-15 (can slide to 10/20 if procurement/NDAs delay)
- Redwood responsibilities:
  - Deliver benchmark harness and baseline numbers for shortlisted models (Aditya)
  - Provide quantized variant runs and throughput estimates on Dedicated pool (Dev)
  - Host a kickoff to align evaluation dataset and acceptance criteria
- Acme responsibilities:
  - Provide redacted evaluation dataset + 1-2 production prompt sets (Jane)
  - Grant temporary test account or sample API keys (Tom/Procurement)
  - Confirm success criteria and target close date
- Dependencies:
  - NDA + procurement for any dedicated test capacity (Procurement)
  - Access to sample dataset and SSO test users

Benchmark success criteria (draft)
- Generative quality: pass >= 85% of prompt-level acceptance checks on Acme eval set (we'll formalize checklist)
- Latency targets (p95)
  - Hosted (managed): <= 150 ms for short (<256 tokens) interactive queries
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU): <= 120 ms p95 for same profile
- Cost targets (ballpark for evaluation; refined after first runs):
  - Target effective inference cost <= $0.003/token for the final production config (we will provide per-model and per-quantization estimates)
- Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent low-latency sessions in Dedicated test pool

Model shortlist (initial) — we will run identical prompts across variants:
- Mistral-Instruct-22B (float/quantized)
- Llama2-70B-Chat (int8/quantized)
- RedWave-64B-Chat (quantized)
- OpenAssistant-30B (baseline smaller model)

Next steps
1) Please review MAP draft and the technical eval milestone in the attachment and confirm the target completion date (proposed 2026-10-15).
2) Jane/Tom: share the redacted eval dataset link and procurement contact for any capacity booking.
3) We'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff (we propose Tue 2026-10-06 10:00 PT).

Attachments: acme_map_draft_v2.xlsx, redwood_latency_bench_template.csv

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once I hear availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Quick technical notes to feed into the MAP before the kickoff:
- Model shortlist: agree with Marissa's list — will add 2 quantized variants per model (int8, nf4) so we can compare quality vs perf/cost.
- Latency targets: let's tighten to p95 <= 100 ms on Dedicated for short queries (<=256 tokens) and <= 150 ms hosted as a realistic expectation. We can call out separate profiles for longer sequences.
- Cost guidance (initial): for quantized models on Dedicated, expect ~50-60% reduction vs float baselines. I'll produce a back-of-envelope $/1M-token estimate for each model ahead of the kickoff.
- Benchmark harness: I'll prepare the JMH-style harness results template (redwood_latency_bench_template.csv) and include instructions for ingesting Acme's test prompts.

I'll attach the cost estimates and sample run plan to the kickoff invite.

- Aditya
